stem:
Meena fills a balloon with air and ties its mouth tightly. She then places the balloon inside a freezer for some time.

The balloon shrinks slightly.

What happens to the density of the air inside the balloon?

options.text: It increases, because cooling brings the air particles closer together, reducing the volume.
It decreases, because cooling always decreases the density of a gas.
It stays the same, because the amount of air in the balloon does not change.
It becomes zero, because cooling stops the movement of air particles.

teacher.key_rationale: For a fixed mass of gas in a flexible container, cooling reduces the volume while the mass stays constant, so density (= mass/volume) increases. Option A is correct; C is the trap for students who think density depends only on the amount of substance, ignoring the change in volume with temperature.
